NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday reaffirmed India's commitment to supporting peace efforts in Ukraine and West Asia during bilateral talks with his Polish counterpart Donald Tusk, as the two countries agreed to deepen cooperation across strategic sectors amid growing global instability.The leaders held wide-ranging talks at Hyderabad House in New Delhi, exploring avenues for cooperation in defence, space, nuclear energy, critical minerals, green technologies and artificial intelligence (AI).They also discussed regional and global developments and agreed to work towards doubling bilateral trade by 2030.Tusk is on a three-day visit to India amid renewed international efforts to end the war in Ukraine.Announcing the decisions taken during the talks, PM Modi said India and Poland would expand cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy, while encouraging Polish companies to participate in joint projects."Today we have agreed to deepen ties in defence, space, and nuclear energy. We invite Polish companies to engage in co-development and co-production with India in all these strategic areas," PM Modi said."In critical minerals and coal gasification too, we will develop new partnerships with Polish expertise," he added.The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said the discussions aimed to build on the strategic partnership established between the two countries in 2024 and expand cooperation across several areas."A new phase in the India-Poland Strategic Partnership. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Prime Minister Donald Tusk of Poland held wide-ranging talks today. Building on the Strategic Partnership established in 2024, the leaders explored new avenues of cooperation in areas including AI, green technologies, critical minerals and defence, while further deepening ties in trade, investment, education, culture and people-to-people exchanges. "The two leaders also reaffirmed their commitment to a rules-based international order and reforms of global institutions, including the United Nations Security Council (UNSC).PM Modi highlighted the growing economic engagement between the two countries, describing India and Poland as emerging centres of growth, technology and innovation amid global uncertainty."The world is going through a period of uncertainty and change. Even at this time, both India and Poland are emerging as important centres of growth, technology, and innovation," he said.He said the growing economic strength of both countries had created new opportunities for bilateral cooperation, with the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) expected to further expand trade and investment."And the India-European Union free trade agreement has further expanded these opportunities. Upon entry into force, this agreement will open up new opportunities for exports of machinery, chemicals, plastics, and engineering goods from India to Poland," he said."Additionally, we will attract new investments from Poland in sectors such as railways and mobility, advanced manufacturing, food processing, and biotech," he added.PM Modi also expressed confidence that the two countries would work together to develop trusted global supply chains and achieve their shared goal of doubling bilateral trade by 2030.The MEA underlined the importance of the India-EU FTA in strengthening economic engagement."Both leaders agreed to work together to double bilateral trade by 2030. The leaders underscored the importance of the India-EU FTA, which is set to unlock new opportunities for businesses and industries, giving fresh impetus to economic engagement. The two leaders also exchanged views on regional and global developments, reaffirming their commitment to a rules-based international order and reform of global institutions, including the UN Security Council," it said in a statement on X.PM Modi said the friendship between India and Poland was rooted not only in diplomatic relations but also in a shared legacy of humanity and compassion."During World War II, the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur sheltered thousands of Polish children and families in India. Poland also extended this spirit of humanity by supporting the safe return of our students from Ukraine in 2022," he added.Earlier on Thursday, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met Tusk and discussed ways to deepen cooperation between India and Poland across various sectors."Pleased to call on Prime Minister Donald Tusk of Poland. Appreciated his sharing thoughts on deepening India-Poland cooperation across a wide range of domains," Jaishankar said in a post on X.Tusk arrived in New Delhi on Wednesday evening for a three-day official visit aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation in defence, trade and strategic sectors. He was received at the airport by Union Minister of State for Food Processing Industries and Jal Shakti Raj Bhushan Choudhary.Welcoming the Polish leader, the MEA said the visit would provide fresh momentum to bilateral ties."A warm welcome to Prime Minister Donald Tusk of Poland on his arrival in New Delhi. He was received at the airport by MoS Raj Bhushan Choudhary. The visit will provide fresh impetus to the India-Poland Strategic Partnership and further deepen our longstanding ties," the MEA posted on X.Tusk is accompanied by Poland's Minister of Finance and Economy, Andrzej Domanski, and a high-level business delegation.According to the MEA, this is Tusk's second visit to India as Polish prime minister, following his earlier visit in 2010.
Article Summary: PM Modi reaffirms support for peace in Ukraine, West Asia as India and Poland deepen strategic ties. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Prime Minister Donald Tusk of Poland held wide-ranging talks today. The leaders explored new avenues of cooperation in areas including AI, green technologies, critical minerals and defence.

Article Title: 'Congress spreading anarchy': BJP draws parallel between France and Delhi protests
Article Text:
BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia

NEW DELHI: BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia on Thursday questioned Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s alleged links with foreign-based organisations, including Progressive International and Indian Alliance Paris, accusing them of amplifying protests in India and alleging a wider conspiracy to create “anarchy and chaos” in the country.Addressing a press conference, Bhatia repeatedly referred to Gandhi as “Rahul Gaddar” and alleged that the Congress leadership’s engagement with international groups raised questions about their activities, funding and possible coordination with protests in India. His remarks followed a Fox News Digital investigation that claimed to have identified 101 organisations across nine countries involved in organising, coordinating or amplifying demonstrations.“The subject is the model of anarchy, chaos, and treachery that the Leader of the Opposition, Rahul Gandhi, is presenting before the country. Now, a news report was published in a very prestigious newspaper today, regarding how these threads of treachery are connecting with foreign agencies,” Bhatia said.“If it is asked, who is the commander-in-chief of this traitor? Who is the leader of this traitor? Then it would not be wrong,” he added.Bhatia cited the report’s references to Indian Alliance Paris, a France-based organisation, alleging that it was among the first to share videos and amplify social media posts concerning Gandhi’s detention during a protest. He questioned whether the organisation’s activities indicated an attempt by foreign-based groups to influence the narrative around India’s domestic political affairs.“This Progressive International organisation describes itself as a transnational anti-capitalist organisation. According to the report I showed, the unrest and vandalism of historical monuments in France, the incidents in Spain, what is happening in India, and the events in Albania are all linked to Progressive International", Bhatia claimed, alleging that the events formed part of a coordinated effort to challenge elected governments and constitutional institutions.“Wherever there is an elected government, they want to overthrow it. They want to destroy constitutional institutions such as the Supreme Court and Parliament, as well as historical buildings..,France, Albania, Spain and Delhi protests — everything is linked", He claimed, referring to a Congress social media post documenting a meeting between Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and a delegation from the organisation at 10 Janpath in New Delhi in April, 2025.“Rahul Gandhi... Rahul the ‘Gaddar’? Does he not have any strength left in him anymore, that now he has to take the help of such agencies and organisations that are anti-India?” Bhatia said.Bhatia also referred to a social media post by Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut about protests in Albania, alleging that it could be interpreted as support for actions against constitutional institutions. He linked this to slogans raised by protesters on the Supreme Court premises, which he claimed were part of a broader attempt to undermine democratic institutions.“Protesting is a fundamental right, but destruction, destroying institutions, arson, and violent demonstrations are not fundamental rights,” Bhatia said.He demanded that Rahul Gandhi and the Congress disclose what was discussed during the meeting with Progressive International, clarify whether any agreement had been reached and explain the sources of funding for the organisations, including whether they had links with foreign individuals or entities.The Fox News Digital report, titled Global Chaos Inc Grows to 101 Groups, also referred to an international coalition of 28 communist and socialist youth organisations allegedly mobilising students for coordinated strikes across Europe. It said the network extended to the US, UK, Greece, Brazil and India, with groups mobilising supporters, calling strikes and amplifying demonstrations through international media outlets.The report also cited the Neville Roy Singham network and Indian Alliance Paris as alleged amplifiers of French demonstrations on social media, drawing parallels with student protests in India. The claims of coordinated efforts to influence protests in India were not independently established by the material cited at the press conference.Bhatia also criticised Rahul’s interactions with British MP Jeremy Corbyn and US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, alleging that their positions on Kashmir were contrary to India’s interests. He accused Rahul of seeking support from organisations he described as anti-India. "Such organisations may be anti-India, but how can the LoP of the country India be anti-India?", he asked.
Article Summary: Gaurav Bhatia questions Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s alleged links with foreign-based organisations, including Progressive International and Indian Alliance Paris. He accuses them of amplifying protests in India and alleging a wider conspiracy to create “anarchy and chaos” in the country.

NEW DELHI: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk on Thursday described Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a “beacon of hope” amid global uncertainty and said he was proud to call him a friend, while highlighting the absence of conflicts of interest between India and Poland as the two countries seek to strengthen their strategic partnership.Addressing a joint press conference with PM Modi at Hyderabad House in New Delhi, Tusk said the two countries had held fruitful discussions on expanding bilateral cooperation and building on the strategic partnership established during Modi’s visit to Poland in August 2024.“We had a fruitful discussion with Prime Minister Modi about how Poland and India can develop and strengthen their strategic partnership. The decision to establish this partnership was made jointly during Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Warsaw in August 2024,” Tusk said.“The synergies between Poland and India are quite clear. We have no conflicts of interest and no historical issues that divide us. We are building our friendship on the basis of trust, shared values, and ideas such as non-violence,” he added.Tusk also drew a parallel between Poland’s Solidarity movement and India’s tradition of non-violence, saying the Polish movement had been inspired by such principles.Praising PM Modi’s role on the global stage, the Polish prime minister said India’s leadership offered hope at a time of geopolitical uncertainty and instability.“Someone like you, Prime Minister, leading a country as powerful as India, is a beacon of hope for all of us. I am very proud, truly proud, to be able to call myself your friend, Mr. Prime Minister,” Tusk said.He also pointed to the economic progress made by both countries over the past 35 years.“Over the past 35 years, both our countries have experienced unprecedented economic success and dynamic growth. Let me put it straightforwardly, without any doubts or hesitation: the world looks upon us with envy, at how India is developing and at Poland’s development,” he said.PM Modi said the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) had expanded opportunities for economic cooperation between India and Poland, building on the momentum in bilateral relations over the past two years.“Our growing economic strength has created new opportunities for the India-Poland partnership. And the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement has made these opportunities even broader,” PM Modi said.The two leaders witnessed the exchange of key memoranda of understanding before addressing the joint press conference.Welcoming Tusk, PM Modi recalled his visit to Poland in 2024, when the two countries elevated their relationship to a strategic partnership.“During that visit, we elevated our relations to the level of a Strategic Partnership. Building on this strong foundation, our partnership has gained new momentum over the past two years,” Modi said.He also highlighted the historical ties between the two countries, describing their friendship as rooted in shared humanity and empathy rather than diplomatic relations alone.“The friendship between India and Poland is not based merely on diplomatic relations, but on the shared heritage of humanity and empathy,” Modi said.Recalling the assistance extended to Polish families during the Second World War, PM Modi said the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur had provided shelter to thousands of Polish children and families in India.The prime minister also said the two sides had agreed to strengthen cooperation in culture, education, sports and tourism. He added that they had discussed regional and global developments, democratic values and the need to reform global governance institutions.“Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort towards peace,” PM Modi said.Tusk arrived in New Delhi on Wednesday for an official visit from October 21 to 23, at PM Modi’s invitation. He is accompanied by Poland’s minister of finance and economy Andrzej Domanski and a business delegation.The two prime ministers held delegation-level talks at Hyderabad House to review bilateral relations and explore cooperation across trade, defence, technology, space and other areas.India’s delegation included external affairs minister S Jaishankar, national security adviser Ajit Doval and foreign secretary Vikram Misri.Earlier on Thursday, Tusk paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat, laying a wreath at the memorial. Jaishankar also called on the Polish prime minister to discuss ways to deepen bilateral cooperation.In a post on X, Jaishankar said, “Pleased to call on Prime Minister Donald Tusk @donaldtuskof Poland. Appreciated his sharing thoughts on deepening India - Poland cooperation across a wide range of domains.”During his visit, Tusk is scheduled to attend the India-Poland Business Forum in New Delhi before travelling to Bengaluru on October 23 for engagements with leaders from India’s information technology and space sectors.Former Polish ambassador to India Adam Burakowski has said both countries aim to increase annual bilateral trade from approximately $6 billion to $10 billion.He has also identified defence and space technology as key areas for cooperation and pointed to the India-EU trade agreement as an opportunity to expand economic engagement.Tusk’s visit marks the first visit by a Polish prime minister to India since 2010. Article Title: State by state, some SIR hurdles are falling
Article Text:
SIR 2026 in Jhahhar

From queues to doorsteps

Then vs now

Less searching through old rolls

Chhattisgarh SIR drive

Finding the voters left out

When the usual apers are missing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

With inputs from Arvind Chauhan, Kaushik Pradhan, Nisha Nambiar, Alok K N Mishra, Abhay Singh, Saptarshi Banerjee, Ashok Pradhan, Kautilya Singh, Lisa Monteiro, Amarjeet Singh, Rashmi Drolia, Navjeeven Gopal, Manvir Saini, Sreerag P S, K Krishnachand, Jignesh Parmar and Kapil Dave

For booth-level officers in Goa, enrolling a voter no longer involves one particularly tedious search: tracing the elector or a parent in the electoral rolls of 2002. That requirement has gone from the current registration process. The papers needed to establish eligibility have not.In Dehradun, Vibhanshu Bhatt, the BLO for Ajabpur, says a wider choice of supporting documents has made it easier to answer voters’ questions. A retired govt employee, for instance, can now offer documents other than a pension letter to establish their status.“With voters now having more options, it has become easier for us to deal with public queries and concerns,” he said.Across several states, BLOs are returning to households, collecting documents to resolve notices issued during the special intensive revision (SIR), and helping eligible voters left out of the rolls apply for re-inclusion. Some are working with a wider range of evidence. Others are helping applicants through the regular registration process, without the additional declarations or links to old rolls required during SIR.The states are at different stages, with officers handling pending verification, fresh enrolment or preparations for special summary revision (SSR). Nor has every state relaxed its documentary requirements. What connects much of the fieldwork is a more active effort to reach voters and help them complete the process.In Delhi, voters served notices because their details contained discrepancies or could not be linked to the 2002 roll no longer have to routinely queue for physical hearings at electoral offices. BLOs visit their homes and collect supporting papers. Assistant electoral registration officers can dispose of cases without formal hearings where the verification is sufficient.For daily-wage earners, the earlier visits to election offices meant losing work. Minor spelling differences, such as Narendra and Narender, are now being corrected without extensive documentation, officials said.“Officials have been directed to facilitate eligible voters rather than reject cases over procedural difficulties. However, prescribed eligibility requirements and documents remain applicable and BLOs do see documents such as birth certificate, passport wherever applicable before submitting declaration forms recommending disposal of cases,” an official said.By October 16, around 25 lakh of Delhi’s 33 lakh SIR notices had been resolved, against around 4 lakh by September 29.In Maharashtra , the BLO mobile application now has an “Other/Equivalent” option. Added after a proposal from chief electoral officer S Chockalingam, it allows supporting evidence beyond the 13 categories originally prescribed to be submitted for scrutiny.The provision is intended to help, among others, homeless people, particularly vulnerable tribal groups and sex workers who may lack the specified papers. Electoral registration officers (EROs) and assistant EROs assess the relevance and validity of the evidence.The numbers are substantial. Maharashtra issued notices to about 1.22 crore electors: roughly 59.76 lakh whose records could not be mapped to the previous roll and 62.48 lakh over logical discrepancies.BLOs can collect documents during home visits and upload them on ECINET for scrutiny. Where the evidence resolves the discrepancy, a routine personal hearing is no longer necessary. Further hearings can still be held when verification requires them.In Ahmedabad, engineering student Krisha Patel found that enrolling as a new voter required fewer papers than some of her friends had been asked to produce.“Unlike some of my friends who were asked to submit proof that their father or grandfather was a voter, I was asked to submit basic documents like Aadhaar card, birth certificate and photos.”Gujarat chief electoral officer Sandip Sagale said BLOs had been instructed to follow revised EC guidelines issued on Oct 15.“The documents establishing the relation of applicants to parents and grandparents are no longer mandatory according to the revised ECI guidelines. Registrations by first-time voters are very encouraging.”In Uttar Pradesh, chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa says current enrolment uses the regular statutory Form 6. Applicants no longer have to establish links with the 2003 rolls through their own names or those of parents or relatives.This is a return to the standard registration procedure after SIR, rather than a new nationwide concession. Rinwa said the original statutory Form 6 is being used during continuous updating of the rolls and will continue during SSR beginning Nov 12.Madhya Pradesh has also instructed district election officials not to seek a separate declaration with Form 6. Applicants must still provide the prescribed identity and address documents and make the form’s standard declaration that their information is true to the best of their knowledge.In Bengal’s current special enrolment drive, an official from the chief electoral officer’s office said applicants need not submit Annexure IV, the declaration used to establish family links with existing or previous rolls. BLOs continue to accept documents from the EC’s prescribed list.For Goa’s BLOs, removing the search through the 2002 roll eliminates a difficult step. But they say the documents for enrolment under Form 6 remain the same, whether someone is applying for the first time or seeking inclusion after deletion during SIR.For another set of BLOs, the immediate task is to return to names that did not make it onto the rolls.In Keralam, a drive that began on Oct 15 involves comparing pre- and post-SIR rolls to identify eligible voters omitted during revision. In Thiruvananthapuram’s Fort ward, BLO N Sajankumar is helping such voters seek inclusion. The exercise also involves checking information on deceased electors against local body databases maintained by the Information Keralam Mission.Chhattisgarh has supplied BLOs with booth-wise lists for a month-long drive to locate eligible omitted voters. They are making household visits, holding polling-station camps twice a week and organising separate camps at educational institutions for young voters.“BLOs are going door to door and, if a person earlier marked absent or shifted is now found, the Form 6 process is facilitated immediately,” a state govt official said. “But the documentary requirements have not been relaxed. The same standard documents applicable to an eligible voter continue to apply.”Completed applications and field-verification reports go to EROs for scrutiny. Finding a person at home does not, by itself, settle the application.In Ahmedabad’s Amraiwadi, special evening camps are scheduled from Oct 21 for night-shelter residents, labourers and homeless citizens, ahead of publication of the draft roll on Nov 12.Bihar is deploying 90,172 BLOs for a drive to enrol left-out voters and first-time applicants, with house-to-house searches and verification of records. The exercise is scheduled to finish by Nov 8.Odisha offers a measure of the additions already made. Since SIR, around 35,000 voters have been added to its rolls. Nearly 1,200 were eligible voters left out during revision; the remainder were newly enrolled voters. BLOs conducted door-to-door visits during a three-day drive from Oct 7 to 9, and registration continues till Oct 31.Delhi’s BLOs, meanwhile, have begun re-verifying 47.6 lakh people categorised as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate after they did not submit enumeration forms and were excluded from the draft rolls. Eligible voters found to have been wrongly excluded will need to apply through Form 6, with assistance from BLOs.In Jharkhand’s Khunti district, two tribal residents who lacked Aadhaar cards and conventional identity and address documents were enrolled after their eligibility was verified through land records, khatian documents and Gram Sabha testimony. Such evidence is subject to scrutiny by electoral registration officers, who decide applications on the basis of records available in each case.Chief electoral officer K Ravi Kumar has directed registration officers not to demand special or additional documents at SIR hearings and to consider available records where conventional proof is unavailable. Alternative verification has also been reported for vulnerable groups, including orphans, destitute women, residents of old-age homes and transgender persons.“Depending on the category, declarations, institutional certificates and field verification may be used,” Kumar said.BLOs can receive the evidence. EROs must examine it before deciding whether an applicant is eligible.In Dehradun’s Gandhigram, BLO Sarthak Srivastava said officers were finishing door-to-door checks of voters left off the roll, who now had more documentary options.In Goa, BLOs say residence proof remains a problem for tenants whose landlords refuse to give NOCs. Applicants must still furnish proof of residence, along with a birth certificate or school-leaving certificate.
Article Summary: BLOs can collect documents during home visits and upload them on ECINET for scrutiny. Applicants no longer have to establish links with their own names through the 2003 rolls. Minor spelling differences, such as Narendra and Narender, are now being corrected without extensive documentation.

Article Title: EC announces bypoll for Madhya Pradesh Rajya Sabha seat vacated by L Murugan
Article Text:
EC announces by-election for Madhya Pradesh Rajya Sabha seat

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission of India (ECI) announced that the by-election to the Rajya Sabha seat from Madhya Pradesh, vacated by former Union minister L Murugan following his resignation, will be held on November 12. The counting of votes will take place on the same day, according to the commission’s press note shared on Thursday.The vacancy arose on October 14, when Murugan resigned from the Rajya Sabha. His term was scheduled to continue until April 2, 2030.According to the schedule announced by the ECI, the notification for the by-election will be issued on October 26. The last date for filing nominations is November 2, while scrutiny of nomination papers will take place on November 3.Candidates will be able to withdraw their nominations until November 5.Polling will be held from 9 am to 4 pm on November 12, with counting scheduled for 5 pm the same day. The election process is to be completed by November 16, the commission said.The commission has specified the procedure for marking preferences on ballot papers, directing that only the integrated violet-coloured sketch pens supplied by the returning officer can be used.The ECI said in its press note, “No other pen shall, under any circumstances, be used in the above said election.”The commission has also said that observers will be appointed to monitor the election process and ensure that it is conducted freely and fairly.“Adequate measures for close monitoring of the election process by appointing observer shall be taken to ensure free and fair election,” the press note stated.
Article Summary: The by-election to the Rajya Sabha seat from Madhya Pradesh will be held on November 12. The seat was vacated by former Union minister L Murugan following his resignation. The election process is to be completed by November 16, the commission said.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Charles Schwab invested an estimated $30 million in a 2,600-acre Montana horse ranch once owned by copper tycoon Marcus Daly to build a private golf club

Charles Schwab invested around $30 million in Montana’s historic Stock Farm

Fly-fishing, dirt roads and casual living shaped Charles Schwab’s Montana escape

Red barns and a private golf course formed part of the Stock Farm project

Stock Farm offered private golf memberships and land lots for sale

Charles Schwab, the discount brokerage businessman, found a reclusive ranch hideaway from his corporate life in Montana’s Bitterroot Valley, where he could enjoy the outdoors, drive along dirt roads, and leave his business suits behind. In the 1990s, he turned his attention to the historic Stock Farm, a 2,600-acre Thoroughbred horse ranch once owned by copper king Marcus Daly.Schwab invested an estimated $30 million in restoring the property and developing a private golf club. The plans included red barns, guest houses, log cabins, and an 18-hole golf course designed by Tom Fazio. According to Forbes, Schwab viewed the project as a personal venture rather than a way to make money, even as golf memberships and land parcels went on sale.Schwab’s decision to invest in the Stock Farm followed a problem with golfing in the Bitterroot Valley. The public golf course in nearby Hamilton was overcrowded and marked by divots, making it less suitable for his 10-handicap game. He responded by putting an estimated $30 million into the 100-year-old, 2,600-acre property, which had belonged to copper king Marcus Daly and operated as a Thoroughbred horse ranch.Schwab wanted to restore the historic property while creating a private golf destination.The Bitterroot Valley, around 35 miles south of Missoula, provided Schwab with a place to step away from his business responsibilities. At the ranch and in the surrounding area, he adopted a more informal routine, going fly-fishing in waders, wearing jeans and driving a brown-and-white 1980 Chevy Suburban along dirt roads.He also regularly ate supper at Cantina La Cocina, a 20-table restaurant in downtown Victor. Scrapping his business suits for jeans, he said, "I wear the Gap denims since I'm on the board."The restoration plans drew on the ranch’s historic character. Schwab intended to build red barns with galvanised-steel roofs, following the style associated with Daly a century earlier. The club buildings and guest houses were planned with clapboard exteriors and pitched single roofs, alongside log cabins with stone bases.A private golf club was central to the development. Tom Fazio, a prominent golf course designer, designed its 18-hole course, which was built in 1999, according to the Montana State Golf Association.The project brought together the restoration of the former horse ranch and the creation of a private recreational facility.The Stock Farm development also included opportunities to buy memberships in the private golf club and land in the surrounding timber highlands. The club offered 350 memberships. By the time Forbes reported on the project in October 1998, 75 memberships had been sold.The development also offered 96 lots ranging from one to 35 acres. Prices were set between $250,000 and $1 million, although only 12 lots had been purchased at the time of the report.Schwab said, "My life is about investing so this is just a unique thing for me to do.”"It's not about making money."
Article Summary: Charles Schwab invested around $30 million in Montana’s historic Stock Farm. The 2,600-acre property had belonged to copper king Marcus Daly and operated as a Thoroughbred horse ranch. The plans included red barns, guest houses, log cabins, and an 18-hole golf course.

Article Title: Season’s Greetings: Delhi sees most polluted day after Dussehra in 5 years, GRAP invoked
Article Text:
Delhi's air quality has worsened, now at an AQI of 245 (Representative image)

GRAP-1 measures kick in





NEW DELHI: Delhi’s air quality deteriorated to poor for the first time this season as the AQI climbed to 245 Wednesday. It was 179 a day earlier.Delhi also saw the most polluted day after Dussehra in the last five years. An AQI higher than Wednesday’s was last recorded in 2021, when it was 284 the day after Dussehra.The air quality worsened due to unfavourable meteorological conditions and additional emissions from firecrackers that were burst during Dussehra celebrations. The contribution of stubble burning to Delhi’s PM2.5 was 3.9% Wednesday.The deterioration in air quality prompted Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to invoke Stage I of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP).This includes a ban on the entry of intercity and inter-state buses from Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand and J&K that are below BS-VI standards and run on neither electricity nor CNG. Regulations on the use of diesel generator (DG) sets also kicked in.GRAP Stage I also asks for augmenting public transport through CNG and electric buses, metro and RRTS services by inducting an additional fleet and increasing the frequency of service.Delhi Metro will run 20 additional trips from Thursday onwards for all weekdays.“The forecast by India Meteorological Department and Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology has also predicted that AQI will remain in the poor category in the coming days,” CAQM said.The commission added that actions under Stage I of GRAP will be implemented, monitored and reviewed by all the agencies in NCR to ensure that the AQI does not rise further.Central Pollution Control Board’s data shows that air quality showed a rising trend since early Wednesday. The AQI was 227 at 7am and touched 245 at 4pm, when CPCB releases its 24-hour average AQI bulletin. It increased to 248 at 8pm.This year, a higher AQI than 245 was last witnessed on July 24 at 246 in the poor category when dust travelled from Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan towards north-west India.The AQI was in the very poor category at seven locations Wednesday -- Pusa (329), Chandni Chowk (326), Jahangirpuri (313), Punjabi Bagh (312), Patparganj (304), Mandir Marg (303) and Vivek Vihar (302).Mahesh Palawat, vice-president of Skymet Meteorology, said the worsening air quality could be attributed to the Dussehra celebrations, including the burning of the Ravana effigies.“Falling night temperatures and light winds may have further contributed to the deterioration.... Traffic emissions, industrial smoke and dust tend to accumulate under such conditions, while fireworks during the celebrations may also have contributed to the overnight rise in pollution. The haze observed Wednesday followed Tuesday’s celebrations,” he said.The Decision Support System (DSS), which functions under the Union ministry of earth sciences, has estimated that the contribution of stubble burning to Delhi’s pollution could rise to 7.4% Thursday, 15.9% Friday and 4.1% Saturday.Sunil Dahiya, founder of the think tank Envirocatalyst, said: “The slow moving wind coming from the northwest, bringing more emission load from farm fires and festive emission load, Tuesday evening to night,” had added to other regional sources as well as emissions from within Delhi.In Oct last year, the AQI worsened to poor on Oct 14. It was 211. It deteriorated to very poor by Oct 20 at 345 last year. Delhi Traffic Police has urged commuters to reduce vehicular emissions. It advised people to use the metro and public transport, carpool and avoid unnecessary trips, maintain their vehicles and keep valid Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCCs).
Article Summary: Delhi also saw the most polluted day after Dussehra in the last five years. The contribution of stubble burning to Delhi’s PM2.5 was 3.9% Wednesday. The deterioration in air quality prompted Commission for Air Quality Management to invoke Stage I of the Graded Response Action Plan.

Article Title: Mumbai clears 77 of 231 garbage hotspots, targets 128 by year-end
Article Text:
BMC is actively addressing garbage-vulnerable points in Mumbai by cleaning and transforming these spaces into public areas.

Continuous monitoring and presence of staff have been established to maintain cleanliness in these improved areas.





MUMBAI: From reclaiming footpaths riddled with illegal construction debris to creating seating areas for senior citizens, BMC is attempting to turn Mumbai's garbage-vulnerable points (GVPs) into usable public spaces.Of the 231 such spots identified across the city till April this year, 77 had been cleaned up by Oct, leaving 154. The civic body has set a target of bringing the number down to 128 by Dec. A garbage-vulnerable point is a location where waste is repeatedly dumped and accumulates over a prolonged period, requiring intervention by the concerned civic ward to address the problem.Two such locations are in Sewri and Chinchpokli areas wherein the civic body is attempting to go beyond simply clearing accumulated waste. At Zakaria Bunder Road along Eastern Freeway, a spot where construction and demolition (C&D) waste was being dumped illegally at night has been cleared, restoring the footpath for safer and more convenient pedestrian movement.A CCTV now has been placed there as well. Shiv Sena UBT corporator Bharti Pednekar said at Chinchpokli, another GVP has been eliminated and the space converted into a seating area, with benches now placed at the site."The facility gives elderly residents a place to sit, relax and interact with one another. We have even spoken to the locals to ensure they dispose waste the correct way," she said.However, sustaining these improvements remains a challenge, particularly in neighbourhoods where dumping garbage at the same location has become a long-standing practice. Assistant Municipal Commissioner of F-South ward Vrushali Ingole said eliminating GVPs requires residents to cooperate with the civic body and hand over their waste directly to BMC collection vans rather than dumping it on roadsides."The ward first deploys staff at an identified spot for a few days to understand where the garbage is coming from. Our teams then approach residents in the surrounding areas, explain the need to stop dumping waste at the location and seek their cooperation. We have also arranged for collection vans to stop at convenient points so residents can hand over their garbage directly," she said.Sanjay Mohite, assistant engineer of F-South's solid waste department, said at the Eastern Freeway location, the ward set up a Solid Waste Management chowky to ensure staff presence and prevent the spot from reverting to a dumping ground. "The footpath was also improved and greenery added to discourage fresh dumping. "Sustained monitoring and public cooperation will be crucial to keeping the spaces clean," said deputy municipal commissioner Kiran Dighavkar.
Article Summary: BMC is attempting to turn Mumbai's garbage-vulnerable points (GVPs) into usable public spaces. Of 231 such spots identified across the city till April this year, 77 had been cleaned up by Oct, leaving 154. The civic body has set a target of bringing the number down to 128 by Dec.

Article Title: CM Devendra Fadnavis announces mega chemical park near Vadhvan Port, seeks Centre’s nod for 2,500-5,000 acres in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has revealed plans for a significant chemical park adjacent to Vadhvan Port





MUMBAI: Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has announced plans for a mega chemical park near Vadhvan Port and urged the Centre to approve the project, for which the state government is willing to allot between 2,500 and 5,000 acres.Speaking at the inauguration of Indochem in Goregaon, Fadnavis said the state government would make the land available for the proposed park and asked the Centre to sanction the project.The proposed location is significant as Dahanu taluka in Palghar district was previously designated an ecologically sensitive zone.Union minister for chemicals and fertilisers JP Nadda said the Centre had already announced the Bhavya Rasayan scheme in the Union Budget. Under the scheme, the Centre will provide Rs 1,000 crore, while the state government will contribute Rs 500 crore.Nadda said the Centre would facilitate environmental clearances for the scheme.The proposed initiative is part of the Centre’s Viksit Bharat vision and its goal of building a $1 trillion economy by 2040.
Article Summary: Devendra Fadnavis has announced plans for a mega chemical park near Vadhvan Port. The state government is willing to allot between 2,500 and 5,000 acres for the project. The proposed location is significant as Dahanu taluka in Palghar district was previously designated an ecologically sensitive zone.

Article Title: CBI arrests SFIO deputy director, advocate in Rs 1 crore bribe case linked to DHFL scam probe
Article Text:
The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. (Representative image)





CHENNAI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has arrested a deputy director-level officer of the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, posted in Chennai, a Delhi-based advocate and the advocate’s relative for allegedly demanding a Rs 1 crore bribe to favour a complainant in an investigation into the DHFL scam.The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch who is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai, advocate Bharat Sharma of New Delhi, and Aryan Sharma, a relative of the advocate, after laying a trap. The arrests followed the advocate’s alleged receipt of Rs 20 lakh from the complainant as part payment of the demanded bribe on behalf of the SFIO officer.According to the CBI, the case was registered against Tanwar, the advocate and others following allegations that they had demanded Rs 1 crore from the complainant to allegedly favour him in an investigation into the DHFL scam being conducted by the SFIO.The CBI verified the complaint before registering the case on Tuesday. It subsequently laid a trap and arrested the three accused after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant on behalf of the SFIO officer.The CBI also conducted searches at the premises of the public servant and the advocate and recovered incriminating material related to the case.The case has been registered under Section 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, relating to criminal conspiracy, and Sections 7 and 7A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Article Summary: The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. Tanwar is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai. The CBI laid a trap after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant.

Article Title: Google’s Ex-CEO Eric Schmidt sees China behind the US in the AI race by at least 6 months, but is still impressed by Chinese …
Article Text:
Eric Schmidt ‘If they’re six months behind, we’re already losing’

Google’s ex-CEO points to smuggled chips and AI distillation

AI is not a bubble, says Eric Schmidt

Price may matter more than performance

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says China trails the US in artificial intelligence by roughly six months, but he warns that the gap may not guarantee an American win. Talking about the intensifying global AI competition, Schmidt said that China is only about six months behind the US in AI capabilities. Along with this, he also warned that the country’s focus on making low-cost and free AI products could enable it to dominate the global adoption. Schmidt believes that if the Chinese AI companies continue to offer powerful AI models at little of no cost, then they could easily gain a huge and significant advantage in developing markets which will incur pressure on the business model of leading AI companies in the US.As reported by Benzinga, speaking on the In Good Company podcast hosted by Nicolai Tangen, CEO of Norges Bank Investment Management, Schmidt said China's position in the AI race is much stronger than many in the West may believe. He argued that even if Chinese AI firms remain slightly behind the technological frontier, their strategy of offering inexpensive or free AI services could help them win users at a global scale.“I don’t know that they will get ahead, but I will tell you that if they’re six months behind, then we’re already losing because their strategy is that the products are free,” Schmidt said.Schmidt noted that many Chinese AI models are either free or significantly cheaper than their Western counterparts.Combined with the growing popularity of open-weight models, this pricing strategy could make Chinese AI offerings particularly attractive in emerging economies where businesses and consumers may not be able to afford premium AI subscriptions.The former Google chief also discussed how China has rapidly reduced the AI gap despite US export restrictions on advanced semiconductor technology. Schmidt said some of China's progress may have been enabled by access to cutting-edge chips that the country was “not supposed to have,” suggesting that some hardware may have been “pilfered or smuggled” into the country.Another factor, he said, is the use of AI distillation techniques, in which developers query advanced AI systems and use the generated responses to train their own models. Such approaches, combined with software innovation, have helped Chinese companies narrow what was once viewed as a much larger technological gap.Schmidt has previously said that China was one to two years behind the US in AI development. He now believes the gap has shrunk to less than six months, highlighting the speed at which Chinese AI firms have progressedDespite growing concerns over the massive sums being invested in artificial intelligence, Schmidt dismissed suggestions that the industry is experiencing a speculative bubble. The technology investor, who owns a stake in Anthropic, argued that the sector's financial performance demonstrates real customer demand rather than hype-driven growth.Pointing to Anthropic's rapid expansion, Schmidt said the company has achieved revenue growth at a pace that exceeds what Google experienced during his tenure as CEO.“That’s real growth. It’s not fake. It’s real money, with real customers who are paying for something useful,” he said.Schmidt's comments come amid an increasingly common view in the AI industry that affordability could become a bigger competitive factor than having the absolute most advanced model. While frontier AI systems continue to grab headlines, many businesses are primarily interested in practical tools that deliver acceptable performance at a reasonable cost.To illustrate the point, Schmidt highlighted a WeChat AI agent developed by Tencent Holdings that can scan medicine packaging and quickly provide personalised guidance. The example, he said, shows how AI systems do not necessarily need to be the most sophisticated models available to deliver meaningful value to users.He added that businesses evaluating AI investments often compare the cost of adopting AI tools with the cost of hiring additional employees, making pricing a critical consideration for enterprise adoption.
Article Summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says China trails the US in artificial intelligence by roughly six months. But he warns that the gap may not guarantee an American win. Schmidt said China's focus on making low-cost and free AI products could enable it to dominate the global adoption.

Article Title: Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026 sees surge in home upgrades, demand grows beyond metros
Article Text: Home upgrades have emerged as one of the biggest shopping trends during the ongoing Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026, with shopping volumes growing more than threefold as consumers invest in kitchen appliances, smart home products, entertainment devices and large household appliances ahead of Diwali.According to Amazon India, growth is increasingly being driven by smaller cities, with non-metro markets accounting for more than 60% of shopping volumes and expanding at twice the rate of metro cities. Cities such as Lucknow, Jaipur, Patna, Guwahati, Coimbatore, Nagpur, Indore and Kochi are leading demand, as customers increasingly explore new product categories and upgrade to premium appliances.Commenting on the trend, Aman Deep Lohan, Director, Home, Kitchen and Outdoors at Amazon India, said consumers are showing growing confidence in upgrading their homes with technology-focused products, while affordability options such as no-cost EMI, exchange offers and instant bank discounts are helping shoppers make larger purchases.According to the company, AI-powered cooking appliances, robotic vacuum cleaners, air purifiers and connected lighting products are among the key categories witnessing increased demand during the festive sale.Amazon also highlighted the role of its AI shopping assistant Rufus, which allows customers to search for products using natural language queries in multiple Indian languages, including Hinglish.Air fryers, refrigerators and dishwashers see strong growthThe company said the kitchen appliances category is currently growing at 3.4 times its average daily pace, with smart and small appliances recording growth of 4.5 times. Air fryers have emerged among the fastest-growing products, operating at 7.5 times their average-day sales pace, while ovens are growing at 5.2 times. Brands such as Philips and SharkNinja have reported growth of more than seven times compared with regular sales periods. Premium refrigerators are also witnessing strong traction. Refrigerators with capacities above 300 litres are selling at 34 times their average-day pace, led by frost-free and side-by-side models from Samsung, LG, Haier and Bosch. Amazon said the Samsung 653-litre AI-enabled side-by-side refrigerator is operating at 33 times its average-day pace.Other lifestyle-oriented kitchen categories are gaining momentum as well, with dishwashers growing sevenfold and chimneys sixfold compared with normal sales levels.Smart TVs, robotic cleaners and connected lighting gain popularityThe living room category is also seeing significant upgrades as consumers opt for larger screens and connected devices. According to Amazon, home entertainment products, including smart TVs and speakers, are running at 37 times their average-day sales pace, with smart TVs accounting for nearly 65% of the category's growth.Brands including Samsung, Xiaomi and TCL have collectively grown 56 times compared with average sales levels, while Indian brand Lumio recorded a 42-fold increase. Robotic vacuum cleaners are another fast-growing category, with sales running at 9.2 times normal levels. Brands such as Ecovacs and Dreame are among the key beneficiaries of this trend. Demand for air purifiers has increased 5.2 times, while smart fans have grown fourfold. Indian smart fan maker Atomberg has reported a fivefold increase in sales during the festive period. Connected lighting products from brands including Philips and Wipro are also seeing strong demand as consumers prepare their homes for Diwali celebrations.Premium appliances and financing options fuel upgradesAmazon said customers are increasingly upgrading to premium and energy-efficient appliances rather than simply replacing existing products. Home appliance sales have grown 25 times during the early stages of the festival sale. Washer-dryers are growing at 18 times their average pace, while premium front-load washing machines continue to gain popularity. LG emerged as the best-selling washing machine brand, recording 17 times its regular-day sales.Air conditioners with four-star and five-star energy ratings are also witnessing strong adoption, growing 15 times faster than normal sales levels. Brands such as Panasonic, Hitachi and Daikin are among the leading sellers in the category. The company said financing options, including exchange discounts, instant bank offers and no-cost EMI plans starting at ₹99 per day, are helping drive the premiumisation trend.AI tools helping customers discover productsAmazon said more than six million customers have used its Deal Alerts feature, which allows shoppers to track prices and receive notifications when products reach preferred price points. The company has also expanded AI-powered shopping tools, including Rufus, Lens AI, AI Review Highlights, Quick View, Buying Guides and personalised product recommendations, to simplify product discovery and comparison.Festival offers continue through DiwaliThe Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026 sale will continue throughout the festive season, with the company offering discounts of up to 50% on more than one lakh products and its lowest prices of the year on over two lakh products across categories including Home, Kitchen, Toys and Outdoors. Customers can also avail a 10% instant discount on purchases made using Axis Bank and ICICI Bank credit cards and EMI transactions, along with additional benefits for Prime members and Amazon Pay users.
Article Summary: Growth is increasingly being driven by smaller cities, with non-metro markets accounting for more than 60% of shopping volumes. Cities such as Lucknow, Jaipur, Patna, Guwahati, Coimbatore, Nagpur, Indore and Kochi are leading demand.Premium appliances and financing options fuel upgrades.

Article Title: Microsoft’s next-generation Xbox may launch after 2028: Here is how much it may cost
Article Text:
Microsoft Project Helix (Representational image)

New leadership and hardware realities

What is Microsoft's Project ‘ Xbox Helix ’

Gamers must brace for expensive computing hardware over the next few years, specifically for flagship consoles. According to a report by Fortune, internal Microsoft estimates project that the next-generation Xbox could cost between $1,200 and $1,800. On top of the potential pricing spike, the system may not hit store shelves until 2028. Notably, at an $1,800 ceiling, the upcoming console would cost nearly four times as much as its predecessor did at launch. This comes as industry rumours suggest Sony’s anticipated PlayStation 6 could also climb upwards of $1,000.The price and launch timeline come at a time when Microsoft’s gaming division is undergoing a period of major restructuring, marked by additional workforce layoffs and the appointment of Asha Sharma as the new chief executive officer (CEO) of Xbox. Sharma has laid out targets for the brand, including scaling Xbox into a billion-player-a-day platform.Meanwhile, persistent global hardware inflation is challenging the standard business model. Microsoft itself believes it’s no longer feasible to develop a high-performance machine that boasts flagship capabilities and fits in the traditional consumer-friendly price tags.For players seeking a more wallet-friendly entry point, Microsoft may offer an alternative ahead of its flagship living-room hardware.Sharma told Fortune that an official next-generation Xbox handheld is planned for release in time for the holiday 2027 shopping season.While launching the portable device in late 2027 gives global component volatility some breathing room, major technology manufacturers widely anticipate that industry-wide memory shortages will linger well into 2028.The persistent supply snags present a major hurdle for the upcoming home console, codenamed Xbox Helix. Microsoft will need to lock down final architectural choices and commit to massive component orders ahead of high-volume mass production – an operational milestone anticipated for late 2027 or early 2028. The surging costs of raw silicon, advanced memory modules and specialised fabrication account directly for the eye-watering estimates.While cutting-edge exclusives and next-generation processing muscle will inevitably attract dedicated early adopters, the prospect of a console priced past $1,500 introduces steep commercial risks.
Article Summary: Microsoft's next-generation Xbox could cost as much as $1,800. The system may not hit store shelves until 2028. The price and launch timeline come at a time when Microsoft’s gaming division is undergoing a period of major restructuring, marked by additional workforce layoffs.
